- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from 30d avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 5–7 days to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.5) and price is trending up, model often overestimates continuation; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day high to avoid momentum overfit.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5), model exhibits lagged response; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30d horizon, model consistently underestimates downward moves in low-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment is flat (0.1–0.3) and price is stable, model often overpredicts volatility; reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to reflect low sentiment-driven noise.
